data_output.description: encode(splits) returns (encoded, dimension). encoded["train"] and encoded["valid"] are (features, labels, users), where features is int32 [n, 5] in exact field order [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday], labels is float32 [n], and users is the user_id array in source-row order. encoded["test"] is (features, None, users) with the same feature representation and canonical test source-row order. Each categorical field has an independent training-only vocabulary, one unknown bucket, and a disjoint global offset; dimension is the sum of all field dimensions.

model_input.description: Model receives the int32 globally offset categorical feature matrix from data.py and dimension equal to its embedding/weight-table size. It remains an additive linear scorer whose logits are bias plus the sum of one weight per feature column, trained with the unchanged BCE step.

feature_engineer.objective: Extend the seed categorical feature matrix in data.py with exactly the predeclared request-context fields tab, hour, and weekday, while fitting every vocabulary exclusively from training rows.
required_changes: In data.py, change FIELDS to exactly ["user_id", "video_id", "tab", "hour", "weekday"].
When reading each log row, retain raw "tab" and derive hour solely from raw "hourmin" with the canonical recipe integer floor(numeric hourmin / 100); validate that the derived hour is in 0..23.
Derive weekday solely from raw "date" using the canonical calendar weekday recipe for YYYYMMDD dates, with Monday=0 through Sunday=6.

Make raw(row) return values in the exact FIELDS order: user_id, video_id, tab, derived hour, derived weekday. Do not add any other raw, derived, profile, metadata, outcome, aggregate, or timestamp feature.
Continue to build separate categorical vocabularies from splits["train"] only, reserve one unknown bucket per field, and apply those training vocabularies unchanged to validation and test rows.
Preserve source CSV iteration order and split filtering so encoded validation and test feature rows remain in canonical source-row order.

Ensure test labels are not loaded or retained for training: test split records/encoded output must provide no test ground truth while still providing test features and row count. Training and validation labels remain available as needed for BCE training and validation-only checkpoint selection.
preserve: Keep LABEL as the raw "long_view" training/validation target and preserve the existing date split boundaries.

Keep the encode return shape and global-offset categorical representation usable by the existing additive Model: encoded split entries must still expose features, labels, and users in that order, with test labels represented as None rather than an array.
Do not modify model.py, introduce feature interactions, or change the BCE objective.
coordination_notes: The trainer will consume encoded["test"] as (test_features, None, test_users); it must obtain the test prediction count from len(test_features), never from test labels.
The fixed prediction artifacts require canonical row IDs np.arange(len(features), dtype=np.int64), aligned to the feature row order emitted here.
Use only exact schema fields "tab", "hourmin", and "date". hour and weekday are canonical derived feature names, not source-column aliases.

trainer.objective: Update train.py so the fixed training command always emits canonical validation and test prediction files without consuming test labels, while retaining validation-only early stopping.
required_changes: In train.py, unpack the test encoded split without a test-label variable, e.g. test_features, _, _ = encoded["test"].

Replace the validation prediction save path behavior with an unconditional file named predictions_valid.npz in the directory Path(args.output).parent. Save exactly row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_features), dtype=np.int64) and scores=model.predict(valid_features).

Save the test artifact unconditionally as Path(args.output).parent / "predictions_test.npz". Save exactly row_ids=np.arange(len(test_features), dtype=np.int64) and scores=model.predict(test_features).
Do not inspect, unpack into a usable variable, score, print, or otherwise consume test labels anywhere in train.py.

Retain checkpoint selection and patience logic based solely on within_user_auc(valid_users, valid_labels, predictions); do not add any test-based metric, stopping rule, model selection, or configuration selection.
Update the train.py module docstring if needed to state that it emits both validation and test prediction artifacts.
preserve: Keep the additive Model construction, optimizer hyperparameter reads, shuffled training batches, BCE training calls, and validation-only within_user_auc proxy unchanged.
Keep the existing config.json unchanged; its current keys and values remain the complete training configuration.
Keep --contract-check behavior as a no-artifact interface probe, using only training and validation data.
coordination_notes: data.py will extend feature width from two to five columns and will represent test labels as None; train.py must remain agnostic to feature width.
The required artifact names are predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz regardless of the basename supplied through --output; both files belong in Path(args.output).parent.
row_ids are canonical zero-based positions in the encoded validation/test source-row order, not user IDs or CSV indices.

reasoning: The hypothesis changes only the request-context feature family, so feature_engineer owns the substantive experiment edit. trainer is additionally required because the parent trainer binds test labels solely to determine output length and does not guarantee the required predictions_valid.npz filename. The additive scorer, BCE objective, hyperparameters, and validation-only model selection are otherwise retained. The only added inputs are schema-approved tab plus canonical hour derived from hourmin and weekday derived from date; their vocabularies are fit on training rows only.
